text:
maya: Heads-up — QA found a case where a bulk flag apply wiped a tenant's custom override. Not catastrophic but scary.
aj: ugh. Which API did they call? bulk apply?
zhen: they called POST /v2/configs/apply with `changes: [...]` and included a tenant scope they didn't intend. UI allowed it.
kayla: so two problems: API semantics that make scope implicit, and console UX not clearly showing which tenants will be affected.
maya: exactly. We need an approval + quorum for sensitive scope changes (tenant-wide, quota-affecting, routing). Suggestion: require 2 approvers for > 50% traffic-affecting changes and add auto-dryrun.
aj: thumbs-up for quorum but operationally painful. Can we make an opt-in policy per team? e.g., org-level safety policy that enforces quorum when enabled.
zhen: API-level idea: split endpoint into PATCH /configs/:id (single-flag safe apply) and POST /configs/bulk-apply (explicit dangerous op) which returns a preflight id. Preflight runs simulations and requires approve POST /configs/preflight/:id/approve with approvers.
ethan: Love preflight. What does preflight simulate? token-level routing decisions, quota delta, and a smoke of synthetic requests against canary infra?
maya: at minimum: config diff, preview of effective routing for a sample tenant set, estimated quota change, and telemetry probes (error rate delta & 95p latency) from staging shadowing.
kayla: Console UX: show a red/yellow/green "safety score" and a diff heatmap across affected routes and tenants. Also an explicit checkbox that says "I acknowledge this will affect X tenants".
aj: For automated approvals, maybe allow CI service accounts to auto-approve if preflight metrics are within thresholds for 24h and owners signed off once.
zhen: Implementation notes: need audit log join keys (who approved which preflight id), immutable preflight snapshot, and a rollback token in response.
maya: Ops concern: what about immediate kill-switch? If rollout is in progress, ops should be able to flip a single flag to pause or revert. We already have emergency-pause but it's global. Need granular kill for preflight rollouts.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: created incident template for preflight kill: `/ops pause-preflight <preflight-id>` posts to #eng-oncall and triggers a rollback playbook.
ethan: Telemetry gating: preflight should attach a watch rule (timebound) that auto-triggers rollback if e.g., error-rate +10% sustained for 5m or latency p95 +25% for 10m. These thresholds should be configurable per rollout.
aj: That implies a small runtime change: preflight rollout must tag routes with `rollout_id` and the router should be able to mark tokens as paused when the kill-switch flips.
zhen: router change seems minimal if we already support route-level metadata. We need a safe default: if router can't find rollout_id, continue serving existing config to avoid outages.
kayla: UI detail: show live progress bar during rollout and a "Revert" button with one-click but require confirm + 2FA for orgs with quorum enabled.
maya: Back to API naming: I'd prefer explicit verbs: /configs/preflight (create), /preflight/:id (status), /preflight/:id/execute -> returns rollout handle. Avoid overloading /apply.
ethan: agree. Also add `dry_run: true` param for existing PATCH for quick previews. CLI snippet: ```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v2/configs/preflight" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"changes":[],"scope":"org:acme","sample_tenants": 50}'
```
aj: Security: ensure preflight snapshot is stored in KMS-backed store with limited retention (30d) and accessible only to approvers and auditors.
maya: timeline? We should ship preflight API + console badge + basic rollout tagging in 3 sprints. Ops-bot: coordinate with oncall for the rollback playbook and test plan.
ops-bot: noted. I'll schedule a tabletop drill next week and post sign-up.
kayla: I'll wire up the UI mocks by EOD Friday and attach to the preflight PR.
zhen: I'll draft the API RFC and router changes in a PR tomorrow.
ethan: I'll write the telemetry gating and alert wiring then.
aj: Thanks team. One more: add a small non-blocking banner in the console for orgs without quorum to recommend enabling safety policy.
maya: Perfect. Closing loop: can everyone drop +1 on the RFC thread when ready so we can start implementation? :thumbsup:
